Maria (Sales): Heads up — Nimbus RFI just landed. They want detailed landing-zone / networking answers for a 2-week POC + a Dedicated option. Can we assemble a short checklist they can include in the RFI? cc @Sam (Solutions) @Aj (Security)
Sam (Solutions): Yup. Quick checklist idea: VNet peering vs PrivateLink options, required ports, peering/route diagram, NSG example, KMS options, audit/log delivery, and a short note about latency/SLA expectations. I can draft the network snippet.
Aj (Security): Add: TLS 1.2+ required, customer-managed keys supported (Azure Key Vault for Private), audit logs must be delivered to customer storage account with object-level timestamps. We should call out retention and SIEM integration (Syslog/CEF).
Kevin (Legal): For the RFI include our DPA + SOC2 certificates. If they ask about FedRAMP/IL5 we need to flag that as "advanced compliance" and escalate (not standard). Also confirm data residency guarantees for Dedicated vs Hosted.
Nina (Sales Engineer): Pricing note to include: POC = metered hosted usage (no setup fee typically), Dedicated = reserved capacity with 3mo min commit for predictable throughput. I'll paste a compact pricing row we can share.
Maria (Sales): Perfect. Nimbus specifically asked: "Can you peer into our landing zone? What ports, do we need public endpoints, and can we bring our own KMS/HSM?" They also asked for a sample NSG and a one-page diagram. Need a draft by EOD tomorrow.
Sam (Solutions): For POC we recommend VNet peering (simpler) + a small bastion for admin access. Ports: 443 outbound only for API calls. If they want SSH to model hosts for debug use 22 to bastion only. No public model endpoints by default. Sample NSG snippet below:
```
# NSG sample (conceptual)
Inbound:
- Allow TCP 443 from customer_subnet
- Allow TCP 22 from bastion_ip (admin only)
Deny all other inbound
Outbound:
- Allow TCP 443 to redwood-models.<region>.internal
- Allow TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.com
```
Sam (Solutions): For Private deployments we can support PKCS#11 HSMs or customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault. For Hosted API they can bring keys via cross-account KMS only for certain enterprise plans — need legal signoff.
Aj (Security): KMS detail: Customer-managed keys via AKV with RBAC is supported for Private. For Dedicated we can bind keys to the tenant and rotate daily if requested (rotation automation). HSM: we support Lunasa/Thales via PKCS#11 for on-prem. Also mention encryption-at-rest default AES-256.
Kevin (Legal): Note to include in the RFI response: "Customer data processed for inference; model weights are not stored as customer data and are not exported without notice" — keeps export control concerns clearer. Also include SLA bullets: latency SLO examples, uptime, and support tiers.
Nina (Sales Engineer): Pricing snippet (one-liner): "POC: hosted metered — $X per 1k tokens + infra usage; Dedicated: $Y/month reserved (min 3 mo) + overage at Z%" — I'll send the exact numbers in the doc.
Maria (Sales): Can someone attach the landing-zone diagram and the capability matrix (KMS/HSM, peering, private endpoints, logging, SIEM hooks)? I want one PDF to hand them.
deploy-bot: Uploaded file landing-zone-reference.pdf (2.1MB)
Sam (Solutions): Uploaded capability-matrix.csv (see rows: Hosted / Dedicated / Private; columns: VNet Peering, PrivateLink, BYOK, HSM, Audit Logs, SLA) — pasted quick summary below.
Sam (Solutions): Quick summary (copyable): Hosted: PrivateLink only, BYOK partial, HSM no, Audit logs to customer bucket; Dedicated: VNet peering + PrivateLink, BYOK yes, HSM optional, Audit logs + SIEM; Private: Full BYOK/HSM support, isolated control plane, custom retention.
Aj (Security): Also add IDS/IPS: we require customers to provide network IDS, but we can stream telemetry for detection rules. For POC we provide logs for the 2-week window; for production we can set up continuous streaming.
Maria (Sales): Great. Kevin — can you review the proposed legal paragraph about keys + FedRAMP escalation and confirm language?
Kevin (Legal): Will do. Draft suggestion: "Customer may provision and manage cryptographic keys. Support for HSM-backed keys is available for Dedicated/Private deployments; Hosted support for customer-managed keys requires an enterprise agreement and additional security review."
Maria (Sales): That reads well. I'll assemble the RFI bundle: one-page network diagram (landing-zone-reference.pdf), capability matrix CSV, short legal paragraph, NSG snippet, and pricing row. Target send to Nimbus tomorrow AM unless there are blockers.
Nina (Sales Engineer): I'll prepare the pricing attachment and final matrix this afternoon.
Sam (Solutions): I'll tidy the NSG snippet and export the diagram as PNG.
Aj (Security): I'll add the SIEM/logging bullets and KMS/HSM details.
Kevin (Legal): I'll drop the legal paragraph in the doc and flag FedRAMP if they check that box.
Maria (Sales): Thanks team :thumbsup:
